name: MAX6102EUR+T
title: MAX6100–MAX6107: low-dropout, micropower series voltage references, 1.25 V to 5 V, in 3-pin SOT23
summary: Three-terminal series references in a 3-pin SOT23, offered at eight fixed outputs from 1.25 V to 5 V. Initial accuracy is ±0.4 % or better and the temperature coefficient at most 75 ppm/°C over -40 °C to +85 °C, set by a curvature-corrected design with trimmed thin-film resistors. The part draws about 90 µA, nearly the same at any supply, sources up to 5 mA and sinks up to 2 mA, and needs neither a series resistor nor an output capacitor. MAX6102EUR+T is the 2.500 V member, with 50 mV typical dropout at 1 mA.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit
circuits.description: The reference runs straight from the supply with no series resistor: IN to the supply, GND to ground, and the reference voltage taken at OUT. Both capacitors may be left off. C1 across the input improves the response to fast supply steps; C2 on the output cuts overshoot and undershoot when the load or supply steps.

parts.note: optional; ceramic, as close to IN as possible

parts.value: supply, within the input voltage range of the fitted part

notes: Any member of the MAX6100–MAX6107 family fits U1; the supply must lie in that part's input voltage range.

where.ΔVOUT(max): largest change of output voltage seen across the temperature range

where.VIN: smallest VIN for which VOUT stays within 0.2 % of its reading at VIN = 5.0 V (5.5 V for the MAX6105)

operation.text: A series-mode reference with three terminals. Curvature correction and laser-trimmed thin-film resistors set the accuracy and temperature drift. Compensation is internal, so no compensation capacitor is needed.

Quiescent current is typically 90 µA and changes by no more than 8 µA/V with supply voltage. IN supplies load current only while the load takes it, unlike a shunt reference, whose resistor must carry the largest load current all the time. While the supply is below the minimum input voltage, as during power-up, the part can draw as much as 400 µA above its normal current, and the supply has to deliver that for the part to start reliably.
Input capacitor: 0.1 µF ceramic from IN to GND, close to the pin, for the best line-transient response. It is optional where transient response does not matter.

Stability needs no output capacitor. Any capacitive load is stable at source currents below 200 µA; above 200 µA of source current, a load capacitance of 0.5 nF to 50 nF can make the output unstable. With step changes of load or supply, an output capacitor reduces overshoot and undershoot.
After a trip through the full operating temperature range, the +25 °C output voltage shifts by typically 130 ppm. The cause is uneven package stress on the transistors of the bandgap core.
Settling to within 0.1 % of the final value typically takes 50 µs to 300 µs, depending on output voltage. Running at minimum dropout with maximum load can stretch this to 1.5 ms.
OUT may be shorted to GND or to IN indefinitely while VIN is below 6 V; at VIN of 6 V or more the short is rated for 60 s. Short-circuit current is typically 110 mA to GND and 12 mA to IN.
